answer: The farm's edge is instant scale: a thousand clones minted at the epoch's nadir of difficulty. Break it with retroactive proof-of-prior-work. Full rewards require each identity to reference its own transaction on an external ledger, an onyx-set inscription on Solana say, at least ninety epochs old. History cannot be backdated. A farm must therefore gestate every shell identity for months before it can farm, carrying idle inventory while rewards shift beneath it; the kernel of the defense is turning the attacker's speed into a cost.
